meta.title: Terms of Service
meta.description: The plain-English agreement between you and Vaulto — what the service is, what you agree to, what we commit to, and the rights you keep as a consumer.

hero.heading: Terms of Service
hero.lead: The agreement between you and Vaulto, in plain English. Read it alongside our privacy summary and security overview.

sections.title: What Vaulto is
sections.body: Vaulto is a private vault for the record of what your family owns — assets, liabilities, documents, and the details that go with them — and a place to get ready for life's big moments. It is a record-keeping and preparation tool. It is not a bank, a custodian, an insurer, or a professional adviser. We do not hold your money or your property. We hold the record you build of it.

sections.title: Who you are agreeing with
sections.body: These terms are the agreement between you and Vaulto, which operates myvaulto.com, the Vaulto web app, and the Vaulto apps for iOS and Android. "We" and "us" mean Vaulto; "you" means the person using the service. By creating an account or using Vaulto you accept these terms. If you do not accept them, please do not use the service.

sections.title: Who can use Vaulto
sections.body: You need to be at least 18 years old and able to enter into a binding agreement where you live. One account belongs to one person, and you are responsible for what is done through yours — so keep your sign-in details to yourself, and tell us promptly if you think someone else has them.

sections.title: What you put in, and who owns it
sections.body: Everything you add to your vault stays yours. You keep ownership of your records, photos, scans, and notes. You give us only the permission we need to run the service for you: to store your content, show it back to you, process it to produce the features you ask for, and keep backups. That permission exists so the product can work — it is not a licence to use your content for anything else, and it ends when you delete the content or your account.

sections.title: What you agree not to do
sections.body: Vaulto is for your own records. Please do not:
items: Use the service for anything unlawful, or to hold content you have no right to hold.
Add another person's information without the authority to do so.
Try to break, overload, probe, or work around the service's protections, or reach another person's account or content.
Copy, scrape, resell, or reverse-engineer the service, or use it to build a competing product.
Use the service in a way that harms Vaulto or other people using it.

sections.title: AI features, and what they are not
sections.body: Some Vaulto features use AI: reading a photo to fill in an item for you, estimating what something is worth, reading a walkthrough aloud, and producing an overview of how prepared you are. Those outputs are estimates and prompts to look closer. They are not financial, legal, tax, or insurance advice; they can be wrong or incomplete; and none of them is a valuation to rely on for a transaction, a tax filing, an insurance claim, or a court. Check anything that matters with a qualified professional before you act on it. Which information leaves Vaulto for AI processing, and who processes it, is set out in our privacy summary.

sections.title: Keeping your own copies
sections.body: Vaulto is built so your information is never trapped: you can export a copy of your records together with the photos and scans you uploaded, from Settings, whenever you want. Please do keep your own copies of anything irreplaceable. Vaulto is a record of what you own and a place to prepare — it is not a substitute for the original deeds, policies, certificates, and wills themselves.

sections.title: What it costs
sections.body: Vaulto is free to use today. If we introduce features that cost money, we will say so clearly before you are asked to pay, and you will never be charged for something you have not agreed to.

sections.title: Availability and changes to the product
sections.body: Vaulto is a young product and it changes often. We may add, change, or remove features, and we may take the service down for maintenance. We work to keep it available and quick, but we do not promise uninterrupted or error-free service and we do not offer a guaranteed level of availability. Where a change would meaningfully affect how you use Vaulto, we will give you reasonable notice.

sections.title: Ending the agreement
sections.body: You can stop using Vaulto whenever you like, and you can delete your account and the data in it yourself — see how to delete your account. We may suspend or close an account that breaches these terms, that is being used unlawfully, or where the law requires it; unless we are unable to, we will tell you why and give you a chance to put it right. If we ever discontinue the service, we will give you reasonable notice and a window to export your data first.

sections.title: Our responsibility to you
sections.body: We will provide Vaulto with reasonable care and skill. Beyond that, the service is provided as it is: we do not warrant that it will meet every need, that AI outputs will be accurate, or that content will never be lost — and to the extent the law allows, we are not liable for indirect or consequential loss, for lost profits, or for loss arising from reliance on an estimate or an overview. Nothing here limits liability that cannot be limited by law, including liability for death or personal injury caused by negligence, and for fraud.

sections.title: The rights you keep as a consumer
sections.body: If you use Vaulto as a consumer, you keep every right your local law gives you. In the United Kingdom that includes your rights under the Consumer Rights Act 2015; in Brazil it includes your rights under the Código de Defesa do Consumidor. Where those rights conflict with anything in these terms, those rights win.

sections.title: Changes to these terms
sections.body: When we change these terms we publish the new version on this page with a new date and version number. If a change materially affects your rights, we will tell you — by email or in the app — before it takes effect. Continuing to use Vaulto after a change means you accept the updated terms; if you would rather not, you can delete your account.

sections.title: Governing law
sections.body: These terms are governed by the law of England and Wales, and the courts of England and Wales have jurisdiction. If you are a consumer resident somewhere else, you may also bring proceedings in your country of residence, and the mandatory consumer law of that country continues to apply to you.

finalCta.title: Your records, your rules.
finalCta.body: Start free — export or delete everything whenever you want. No lock-in.
